A growing body of scientiﬁ c evidence suggests that long-term 
improvements in body weight, waist circumference, and CVD
risk factors appear to be determined more by the total number 
of kcal consumed and expended than by the proportion of mac-
ronutrients in the diet.85, 99, 103–105 However, kcal-restricted diets 
with a modest increase in the proportion of kcal from mono-
macronutrient compositions showed that each of the four diets 
modestly reduced body weight, waist circumference, and several
CVD risk factors regardless of the diet that was followed.103
